definitionEn: a film or book that is extremely popular and earns a lot of money
situation: A new film or novel is so popular that it sells millions of tickets or copies.

examples.text: The studio is betting that its latest superhero [[blockbuster]] will earn a billion dollars worldwide.
Her first thriller became a summer [[blockbuster]], selling two million copies in three months.
The drug became a [[blockbuster]] for the company, with annual sales of over five billion dollars.

texts: Cinemas are hoping a big summer [[blockbuster]] will bring audiences back.
The novel was a [[blockbuster]] long before it was turned into a TV series.
Every studio wants the next [[blockbuster]], so original films struggle to get funding.

badCollocation.text: a [[blockbuster]] that nobody went to see
badCollocation.noteRu: Blockbuster — фильм или книга с огромным успехом, а не просто дорогой зрелищный фильм. Провал — a flop.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Снять фильм — make (или shoot) a film. Take off — калька с «снять», но значит «снять одежду» или «взлететь»; remove и write off тоже не подходят.

nuance.text: The summer's biggest [[blockbuster]] earned over a billion dollars at the box office.
nuance.explanationRu: Blockbuster — прежде всего кассовый фильм (box office — кинопрокат). Bestseller — книга, которую раскупают; кассовых сборов у книги нет.

reverse.text: The cookbook stayed at the top of the [[bestseller]] list for six weeks.
reverse.explanationRu: Список самых продаваемых книг — the bestseller list. «Blockbuster list» так не говорят.

fixIt.text: The low-budget horror film was the biggest [[boom]] of the summer, earning over 900 million dollars.
fixIt.explanationRu: Кассовый хит — a blockbuster. Boom — период бурного роста (экономики, продаж), а не отдельный фильм.

definitionEn: to have something impressive that people can be proud of, used about places and things
senseNote: Здесь — «может похвастаться, располагает» (о местах и вещах); значение «хвастаться» проще.
situation: An advert or guidebook describes the impressive features that a hotel, city or product has.

examples.text: Tourists love the little town, which [[boasts]] a medieval castle, two museums and a sandy beach.
The new phone [[boasts]] a battery that lasts two full days on a single charge.
With over fifty galleries, the city [[boasts]] one of the richest art scenes in Europe.

texts: Our new office [[boasts]] stunning views over the river.
The hotel [[boasts]] three restaurants, a spa and a rooftop pool.
This small village [[boasts]] the oldest pub in the country.

badCollocation.noteRu: В значении «располагать» boast берёт прямое дополнение: the hotel boasts a pool. С with так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: О месте, у которого есть чем гордиться, говорят boasts. Brag — только о людях, praise — «хвалить», pride oneself on — «гордиться собой».

nuance.text: The museum [[boasts]] the largest collection of dinosaur bones in the world.
nuance.explanationRu: Brag — хвастаться, о человеке и с неодобрением: he brags about his car. Boast в значении «может похвастаться» говорят о местах и вещах; музей не может brag.

fixIt.text: The resort [[prides]] three golf courses and a private marina.
fixIt.explanationRu: Курорт «может похвастаться» полями для гольфа — boasts. Pride используется только как pride oneself on something.

rewrite.original: The city has more than two hundred parks, which is impressive.
rewrite.frame: The city ____ more than two hundred parks.
rewrite.explanationRu: О том, чем место может гордиться, говорят boast: the city boasts two hundred parks.

definitionEn: a sudden period of fast growth in business, sales or popularity
senseNote: Здесь — «бум, резкий рост» (экономики, продаж, моды); значение «гул, грохот» проще.
situation: Sales, prices or interest in something grow very fast for a period, and many people make money.

examples.text: Cheap loans fuelled a housing [[boom]] that ended in a painful crash.
The online shopping [[boom]] has left many high-street shops empty.
The city saw a [[boom]] in cycling after it built fifty kilometres of new bike lanes.

texts: The post-war baby [[boom]] changed the country for decades.
Nobody expected the [[boom]] in vinyl records to last so long.
During the oil [[boom]], new hotels and shopping malls appeared everywhere.

badCollocation.noteRu: Рост чего-то — a boom in something: a boom in house prices, a boom in tourism. С of так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Резкий рост — a boom in something. Bang — хлопок, blow — удар, blast — взрыв или порыв ветра.

nuance.text: The 1990s saw a technology [[boom]], with new internet companies appearing every week.
nuance.explanationRu: Boom — целый период бурного роста и активности: a technology boom. Rise — рост показателя, и нужен предлог in: a rise in prices. «A technology rise» так не говорят.

reverse.text: There has been a small [[rise]] in unemployment this month.
reverse.explanationRu: Boom — большой и бурный подъём, обычно деловой активности. Небольшой рост безработицы — a small rise.

fixIt.text: The recent [[bloom]] in tourism has created thousands of new jobs on the island.
fixIt.explanationRu: Резкий рост туризма — a boom in tourism. Bloom — «цветение», слова похожи только на слух.

wordFormation.text: Thanks to a [[booming]] economy, unemployment is at its lowest level for decades.

definitionEn: to recover quickly after a failure, illness or difficult period (usually with 'back')
senseNote: Здесь — bounce back «быстро восстановиться»; прямое значение «отскакивать» (о мяче) проще.
situation: After losing a job, a match or their health, someone quickly returns to their normal, successful state.

examples.text: After losing her job, she [[bounced]] back quickly and started her own business within a year.
Tourism [[bounced]] back strongly once the travel restrictions were lifted.
Children usually [[bounce]] back from minor illnesses much faster than adults do.

texts: Don't worry about the kids. They'll [[bounce]] back in no time.
Share prices often [[bounce]] back after a sudden fall.
It took the team a whole season to [[bounce]] back from relegation.

badCollocation.noteRu: Bounce back — непереходный глагол: the economy bounced back. «Оживить» экономику — revive или boost the economy.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Быстро оправиться — bounce back. Bounce up, off и out описывают движение мяча, а не восстановление.

nuance.text: Tourism has [[bounced]] back to pre-crisis levels.
nuance.explanationRu: Bounce back — быстро восстановиться после спада. Return уже значит «вернуться», поэтому return back — тавтология; говорят просто return to pre-crisis levels.

reverse.text: She [[returned]] to work two weeks after the operation.
reverse.explanationRu: Вернуться куда-то — return to. Bounce в значении «восстановиться» употребляется только с back.

fixIt.text: After losing the first two games, the team [[bumped]] back and won the tournament.
fixIt.explanationRu: Быстро оправиться после неудачи — bounce back. Bump — «удариться, стукнуться», с back в этом смысле не используется.

reply.context: A colleague says: "I can't believe I failed my driving test again. I'm useless."
options: Don't be so hard on yourself. You'll bounce back, and loads of people pass on the third try.
Just bounce the test back to the examiner next time!
One anticipates that you shall bounce back in due course.
reply.explanationRu: Bounce back — быстро оправиться после неудачи. Во втором ответе смысл перепутан (нельзя «отбить» экзамен), третий звучит слишком книжно для утешения.

rewrite.original: The economy recovered quickly after the recession.
rewrite.frame: The economy ____ quickly after the recession.

definitionEn: a limit that shows what is acceptable, possible or allowed
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «граница допустимого, предел»; прямое значение — граница участка или территории.
situation: You talk about the limits of acceptable behaviour, or of what art, science or technology can do.

examples.text: Her latest film pushes the [[boundaries]] of what animation can do.
It's healthy to set clear [[boundaries]] with colleagues who message you late at night.
The interviewer crossed a [[boundary]] when she started asking about his children.

texts: Young children need clear [[boundaries]] and consistent rules.
The scientists are pushing the [[boundaries]] of what we know about the brain.
Good friends respect each other's [[boundaries]], even when they disagree.

badCollocation.noteRu: Устанавливать личные границы — set boundaries (или draw boundaries). Put так не используется.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Раздвигать границы возможного — push (или expand) the boundaries. Move apart, open и spread так не говорят.

nuance.text: Good science fiction pushes the [[boundaries]] of our imagination.
nuance.explanationRu: Border — государственная граница между странами. Boundary — любой предел, в том числе переносный: push the boundaries, set boundaries.

reverse.text: It took us two hours to cross the [[border]] into Spain.
reverse.explanationRu: Границу между странами пересекают — cross the border. Boundary так о государственной границе не говорят.

fixIt.text: My new manager has no sense of personal [[borders]]: he reads my messages over my shoulder.
fixIt.explanationRu: Личные границы — personal boundaries. Borders — границы между странами.

reply.context: A friend says: "My mum calls me five times a day and turns up at my flat without warning."
options: Just move abroad. Then there'll be a boundary between you.
Maybe it's time to set some boundaries. Tell her you'll call every evening instead.
One ought to delineate one's personal boundaries with the utmost rigour.
reply.explanationRu: Set boundaries — обозначить личные границы, это и советуют. Первый ответ понимает boundary буквально, третий звучит как учебник, а не как слова друга.

definitionEn: an act of breaking a law, rule, agreement or promise
situation: Someone fails to follow a law, contract or promise, or private data is exposed because security fails.

examples.text: The supplier was sued for [[breach]] of contract after missing three deadlines in a row.
Millions of customers' passwords were exposed in a massive data [[breach]] last year.
Reading your partner's private messages without asking is a serious [[breach]] of trust.

texts: Leaking the report to journalists was a clear [[breach]] of the rules.
The hackers took advantage of a security [[breach]] in the payment system.
Not paying the rent on time is a [[breach]] of your tenancy agreement.

badCollocation.noteRu: Нарушение совершают — commit a breach (или просто breach the rules). Make a breach так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Юридический термин — breach of contract (нарушение договора). Break — «перерыв» или глагол, crack — «трещина», violence — «насилие».

nuance.text: Our lawyer thinks we have a strong case for [[breach]] of contract.
nuance.explanationRu: Breach of contract — устойчивый юридический термин, violation of contract звучит неестественно. Violation чаще о правах и правилах: human rights violations.

reverse.text: He got a ticket for a minor traffic [[violation]].
reverse.explanationRu: Нарушение ПДД — a traffic violation (или offence). «Traffic breach» так не говорят.

fixIt.text: The newspaper admitted that publishing the leaked emails was a [[break]] of confidentiality.
fixIt.explanationRu: Нарушение конфиденциальности — a breach of confidentiality. Break как существительное значит «перерыв» или «разрыв».

reply.context: Your colleague says: "I just got an email saying my card details may have been stolen from an online shop I use."
options: A breach? Great, so your account is extra safe now.
Kindly be informed that a breach has, in all likelihood, transpired.
Sounds like a data breach. Change your password and call the bank right away.
reply.explanationRu: Data breach — утечка данных, поэтому нужно срочно менять пароль. В первом ответе смысл перевёрнут, второй звучит как официальное письмо.

rewrite.original: The company didn't do what the contract said, so it was taken to court.
rewrite.frame: The company was taken to court for ____.

definitionEn: a detailed list that shows how a total amount is divided into parts
senseNote: Здесь — «разбивка, детализация» (a breakdown of costs); значения «поломка» и «нервный срыв» — другие.
situation: You ask for a total, such as a bill or budget, to be shown item by item or by category.

examples.text: Could you send me a [[breakdown]] of the project costs by Friday?
The report includes a [[breakdown]] of sales by region and age group.
My phone bill came with a detailed [[breakdown]] of every call and text I'd made.

texts: The accountant gave us a clear [[breakdown]] of where the money had gone.
Can I see a [[breakdown]] of the survey results by gender?
The invoice has a line-by-line [[breakdown]] of all the charges.

badCollocation.noteRu: Разбивка чего-то — a breakdown of something: a breakdown of the costs. С on так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Разбивка бюджета по статьям — a breakdown. Breakup — расставание, outbreak — вспышка (болезни, войны), breakout — побег.

nuance.text: Please send me a [[breakdown]] of the costs by category.
nuance.explanationRu: Разбивку расходов по статьям называют breakdown. Decomposition — «разложение, гниение» или научный термин; как офисное «декомпозиция» к бюджету не подходит.

fixIt.text: The client asked for a [[breaking]] of the costs by category, not just the total.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Разбивка» расходов — a breakdown. Breaking — это «ломание», а не детализация.

reply.context: Your manager says: "The conference cost twice what we planned. What happened?"
options: Sorry, I had a breakdown of the costs. I cried when I saw the invoice.
I'll send you a breakdown of the costs. The venue alone was forty per cent over budget.
A breakdown shall be furnished posthaste, I assure you.
reply.explanationRu: A breakdown of the costs — детализация расходов, это и нужно. Первый ответ путает её с нервным срывом, третий звучит нелепо официально.

rewrite.original: Can you show me how the total cost is divided into different items?
rewrite.frame: Can you give me ____ of the total cost?
rewrite.explanationRu: Детализация общей суммы по пунктам — a breakdown of the cost.

definitionEn: an important new discovery or development that suddenly makes progress possible
senseNote: Так называют не только научные открытия, но и перелом в переговорах или первый большой успех в карьере.
situation: After a long period of failure, scientists, negotiators or artists suddenly make important progress.

examples.text: Scientists say the new vaccine is a major [[breakthrough]] in the fight against malaria.
After months of deadlock, negotiators finally made a [[breakthrough]] on Friday night.
Her role in the hit TV series was her big [[breakthrough]] as an actress.

texts: The discovery of penicillin was a medical [[breakthrough]] that saved millions of lives.
There has been no [[breakthrough]] in the talks between the two sides.
Therapy finally led to a [[breakthrough]], and he began to talk about his childhood.

badCollocation.noteRu: Прорыв в какой-то области — a breakthrough in something: a breakthrough in medicine. С of так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Совершить прорыв — make (или achieve) a breakthrough. Do, take и break с этим словом не употребляются.

nuance.text: The two companies had argued for a year before a sudden [[breakthrough]] allowed the merger to go ahead.
nuance.explanationRu: Discovery — открытие того, что уже существовало (новый вид, древний корабль). Breakthrough — решающий прорыв после трудностей: в науке, переговорах, карьере.

reverse.text: The [[discovery]] of an ancient ship in the harbour surprised archaeologists.
reverse.explanationRu: Корабль нашли — это discovery (находка, открытие). Breakthrough — прорыв в решении проблемы.

fixIt.text: Researchers have made an important [[breakout]] in the treatment of diabetes.
fixIt.explanationRu: Прорыв в лечении — a breakthrough. Breakout — «побег» (из тюрьмы) или «вспышка».

reply.context: A friend who has been learning Chinese for two years says: "Something clicked this week. I understood a whole film without subtitles!"
options: That's a real breakthrough! All that hard work is finally paying off.
Oh no, a breakthrough? Maybe take a break from studying for a while.
Such a breakthrough is, one must concede, of notable significance.
reply.explanationRu: Breakthrough — долгожданный прорыв, это радостная новость. Во втором ответе смысл перевёрнут, третий звучит слишком официально для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: to cause a feeling or situation, usually a bad one, to develop
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «порождать» (подозрения, недовольство); значение «разводить животных, размножаться» проще.
situation: A bad situation, like secrecy or unfairness, slowly causes negative feelings or problems to grow.

examples.text: Constant secrecy in the office only [[breeds]] suspicion and gossip.
Youth unemployment can [[breed]] resentment and a sense of hopelessness.
Success [[breeds]] confidence, and confident players take more risks.

texts: Familiarity [[breeds]] contempt, as the old saying goes.
Poverty often [[breeds]] crime in neglected neighbourhoods.
A culture of blame [[breeds]] fear, and fear kills creativity.

badCollocation.noteRu: Дискуссию вызывают — spark или provoke a discussion. Breed — медленно порождать негативные чувства: breed resentment.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Постепенно порождать недоверие — breed suspicion. Grow suspicion — калька с «взращивать», bear — «нести, выносить», deliver — «доставлять».

nuance.text: Years of unfair treatment [[bred]] deep resentment among the workers.
nuance.explanationRu: Breed — постепенно порождать чувство (обиду, недоверие). Raise — поднимать вопрос или вызывать опасения: raise concerns; с resentment не сочетается.

reverse.text: The report [[raised]] serious questions about safety.
reverse.explanationRu: Вопросы и опасения «поднимают» — raise questions. Breed описывает медленное развитие чувства.

fixIt.text: Unfair pay can [[grow]] anger and resentment among staff.
fixIt.explanationRu: Порождать недовольство — breed resentment. Grow в таком значении — калька с «взращивать».

wordFormation.text: Badly moderated online forums can become a [[breeding]] ground for hate.

rewrite.original: When people are treated unfairly, they slowly start to feel resentment.
rewrite.explanationRu: Постепенно порождать чувство — breed: unfair treatment breeds resentment.

definitionEn: money or a gift offered to persuade someone to do something dishonest
situation: Someone secretly gives an official money so that they will break the rules for them.

examples.text: The building inspector was jailed for accepting [[bribes]] from construction companies.
He tried to offer the border guard a [[bribe]] to let him through without a visa.
The referee admitted taking a [[bribe]] to fix the result of the match.

texts: She refused the [[bribe]] and reported the official to the police.
In some countries, you still have to pay a [[bribe]] to get a driving licence.
The toy was a small [[bribe]] to keep the kids quiet during the flight.

badCollocation.text: win three [[bribes]] in a card game
badCollocation.noteRu: Взятка в карточной игре — a trick. Bribe — только незаконная плата за нечестную услугу.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Брать взятку — take (или accept) a bribe. Catch, hold и grab так не используются.

nuance.text: The company paid millions in [[bribes]] to win the government contract.
nuance.explanationRu: Bribe — взятка, тайная плата за нечестную услугу. Tip — чаевые, открытая благодарность за хорошее обслуживание; контракты за чаевые не получают.

reverse.text: We left the waiter a generous [[tip]] because the service was excellent.
reverse.explanationRu: Официанту оставляют чаевые — tip. Bribe — незаконная плата, а не благодарность.

fixIt.text: The customs officer was sacked after taking a [[bribery]] from a smuggler.
fixIt.explanationRu: Конкретная взятка — a bribe (исчисляемое). Bribery — взяточничество как явление, с артиклем a не употребляется.

wordFormation.text: He was charged with [[bribery]] after paying a council official to approve his plans.

reply.context: A friend says: "The mechanic said he'd pass my car's safety test if I gave him an extra hundred in cash."
options: Nice, a bribe! Leave him a good review for the service.
Such a bribe would constitute a most regrettable impropriety.
That's a bribe! I'd take the car to another garage.
reply.explanationRu: Деньги за то, чтобы закрыть глаза на неисправности, — bribe, и соглашаться нельзя. Первый ответ путает взятку с чаевыми, второй звучит слишком книжно.

rewrite.original: The businessman secretly paid the official to approve his project.
rewrite.frame: The businessman ____ to approve his project.
rewrite.explanationRu: Дать взятку — pay (или give) someone a bribe.
